source.summary: GitHub Actions 'Embedder footprint' runs for PR #387 (branch fix/114-tailcall-fallback at head a8b99695976516079406aa39e05a4573b8fb9a59 — the #114 loop-dispatch fallback: cargo feature `loop-dispatch-fallback` (default off) makes `call_code` bounce to the trampoline driver `vm::drive_loop_dispatch` instead of dispatching the next handler, with all four interpreter segment entries routed through the driver; plus the op-registry fix that registers `drive_loop_dispatch` with a justified Exact(0) SHAPE_OVERRIDES entry as `call_code`'s fallback counterpart, adds `resume_loop_dispatch` to the registry generator's not_handlers set, and regenerates op_registry.rs; merged with current main at e1be4a9 (PR #384)) (ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45889106469, 45889123389 and 45889141430 against the branch produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series; a three-run control against unmodified main (workflow_dispatch runs 45890660462, 45890676048 and 45890692847) isolates the attribution recorded in the derivation
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #387 (the #114 loop-dispatch fallback and its op-registry fix), following the PR #384 Codex review round-5 re-baseline. Attribution was isolated with a three-run control against unmodified main at e1be4a9 (workflow_dispatch runs 45890660462, 45890676048 and 45890692847; byte-identical across the three, and the size gate passes on main): against main, the branch moves only the eight series of the core-aot and core-jit configurations — in release, core-aot stripped file +496 B and stripped .text +496 B, core-jit stripped file +1,040 B and stripped .text +1,024 B; in release-size, core-aot stripped file +976 B and stripped .text +960 B, core-jit stripped file +1,840 B and stripped .text +1,824 B — while the baseline configuration is byte-identical and every other series measures below main (the interpreter-only and component-linked configurations shrink by 1,536–4,240 B, a codegen/layout effect of the vm.rs dispatch restructure with the feature off). The pull-request run 45889099409 at the same head measured byte-identically to the three branch dispatch runs. Against the checked-in baseline only those eight series grow (release core-aot stripped file +392 B and stripped .text +480 B; release core-jit stripped file +1,040 B and stripped .text +1,024 B; release-size core-aot stripped file +816 B and stripped .text +896 B; release-size core-jit stripped file +1,840 B and stripped .text +1,824 B), so only those eight series are re-baselined to the branch measurements and every other baseline is retained, following the established practice of re-baselining growth only. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the three branch samples and the three main samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth remains the release component stripped file series at +11.67% (2,433,656 B to 2,717,576 B; that series is retained — the branch measures below it), and the re-baselined core-jit release stripped file series stands at +8.37% (1,989,584 B to 2,156,168 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
